Data Storage & External Services

When mock data is disabled, Entity Framework connects to SQL Server LocalDB using integrated security. The shipped configuration sets UseMockData=true, so the default runtime uses the in-memory catalog service. Application Insights is configured for telemetry; no external business APIs, cache, or message broker were identified.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac selects either the in-memory catalog implementation or the Entity Framework implementation based on UseMockData.
  • Entity Framework maps catalog items to required catalog-brand and catalog-type relationships.
  • The application renders HTML pages and does not expose a separate REST API.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining a product catalog, including product types, brands, pricing, and inventory thresholds. Catalog data is served from preconfigured in-memory data by default or from SQL Server when database mode is enabled.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog ManagementProduct available for browsing and maintenanceBelongs to one catalog brand and one catalog type
CatalogBrandCatalog ManagementBrand classification for productsCan be associated with multiple catalog items
CatalogTypeCatalog ManagementType classification for productsCan be associated with multiple catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopLegacyWebFormsCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeOptional SQL Server LocalDB; default mock implementation

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Create a Catalog Item

  1. A user opens the catalog creation page and supplies product details, brand/type, price, and inventory values.
  2. The page checks ModelState; invalid values are not submitted to the catalog service.
  3. CatalogServiceMock assigns an in-memory identifier when mock mode is enabled. Database mode uses the HiLo sequence generator and saves through EF6.
  4. The page redirects to the catalog listing.

Workflow 2: Update or Delete a Catalog Item

  1. A user selects an item from the listing; route data supplies the item identifier.
  2. The edit or delete page loads the item through ICatalogService.
  3. Edit validates the bound form state before calling UpdateCatalogItem; delete calls RemoveCatalogItem.
  4. The user is redirected to the catalog listing after the operation.

Workflow 3: Browse Catalog

The home page retrieves a page of catalog items and binds the item, brand, and type information to the server-rendered list. Paging uses the route's index and size values; the default is page index 0 and page size 10.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No cross-service calls or distributed data aggregation were identified. The catalog page obtains product and lookup data from the same ICatalogService; the active implementation is selected locally by configuration.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User participant Page as "Catalog Create Page" participant Service as "ICatalogService" participant Store as "Mock Store or EF Context" participant Database as "SQL Server LocalDB" User->>Page: Submit product details Page->>Page: Validate model state alt Input is valid Page->>Service: Create catalog item alt Mock data enabled Service->>Store: Assign identifier and append item else Database mode Service->>Store: Allocate HiLo identifier and add entity Store->>Database: Save changes Database-->>Store: Commit result end Service-->>Page: Creation complete Page-->>User: Redirect to catalog listing else Input is invalid Page-->>User: Redisplay validation feedback end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog item price must satisfy its numeric format and range annotations; inventory and restock thresholds have configured numeric ranges.
  • Each database-backed catalog item requires one brand and one type.
  • The application selects mock or database behavior from UseMockData; customization data is separately controlled by UseCustomizationData.
  • Database mode initializes lookup/product seed data and uses SQL sequence values to allocate identifiers.
  • Catalog changes are local to the application; no external business events or compensating transactions were found.
  • No authentication or authorization rules were identified in the assessed application routes.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and depends on older Web Forms, EF6, Bootstrap, and telemetry packages. Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1 is affected by high-severity CVE-2024-21907; the patched version is 13.0.1 or later. NuGet CLI dependency resolution could not load the legacy WebApplication targets, so transitive dependencies were not enumerated.

Notable Observations

  • packages.config lists 44 direct dependencies and no test-scoped packages.
  • The project uses both ASP.NET Web Forms UI libraries and Autofac's older Web Forms integration.
  • AppCAT identified the checked-in connection string as a configuration concern; the connection uses LocalDB and integrated security rather than an embedded password.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The catalog data model contains three entities and is persisted with Entity Framework 6 when database mode is enabled. The default configuration instead uses an in-memory catalog service and preconfigured catalog data.

Caching Strategy

No explicit cache provider, cache annotations, TTL policy, or cache-aside behavior was detected. The mock service retains catalog records in an in-memory list for the process lifetime; this is its backing store rather than a separate cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

All catalog entities are owned by one application and one logical data context. Database mode uses a single LocalDB database; mock mode keeps data in memory. No cross-service data exchange, CQRS, or service-level data isolation was found.
